GRASIM INDUSTRIES Q2 FY27: CONSOLIDATED REVENUE UP 26% YOY, EBITDA RISES 25%, ADJUSTED PAT DECLINES 10%; BIRLA OPUS TARGETS DOUBLE-DIGIT MARKET SHARE IN H2 FY27, BIRLA PIVOT AIMS ₹12,000 CR FY27 REVENUE & CEMENT CAPACITY TARGETED AT 242.9 MTPA BY MARCH 2028

• Paints Business: Birla Opus revenue grew 35% YoY to ₹1,337 Cr, with volumes rising 20%.

• Paints Market Share Guidance: Management expects Birla Opus to cross double-digit revenue market share in H2 FY27.

• Paints Distribution: Crossed 60,000 dealers and 1,760 branded stores, with 11 new products launched during Q2.

• Cement Business: Revenue rose 19% YoY to ₹23,295 Cr, with volumes growing 12.9% to 38.2 million tonnes.

• Cement Capacity Guidance: Targets 242.9 MTPA capacity by March 2028, compared with 210.1 MTPA currently.

• B2B E-Commerce: Birla Pivot revenue surged 66% YoY to ₹2,785 Cr, with management targeting over ₹12,000 Cr revenue in FY27.

• Birla Pivot Profitability: Management expects EBITDA breakeven in H2 FY27, supported by improving gross margins and cost discipline.

• Cellulosic Fibres: Revenue grew 29% YoY to ₹5,344 Cr; 55,000 TPA Lyocell Phase 1 expansion progressing, with Phase 2 planned at 110,000 TPA.

• Chemicals Business: Revenue increased 15% YoY to ₹2,759 Cr, while EBITDA declined 11% due to higher power and input costs.

• Chemicals Expansion: Commissioned 50,000 TPA CPVC and 50,000 TPA Epichlorohydrin facilities; targets 67% chlorine integration by FY27-end.

• Financial Services: Revenue increased 32% YoY to ₹13,990 Cr; lending portfolio grew 32% to ₹2,33,930 Cr.

• FY27 Capex Plan: Standalone capital expenditure planned at ₹3,157 Cr, with ₹1,022 Cr spent during H1 FY27.

• Debt Position: Consolidated net debt excluding financial services borrowings stood at ₹45,756 Cr, with net debt-to-TTM EBITDA at 1.59x.

• Management Outlook: Focused on scaling paints and B2B e-commerce, expanding cement and fibre capacities, improving chemical integration, and strengthening profitability through cost efficiencies.

ASSOCIATED ALCOHOLS & BREWERIES Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 7% YOY, EBITDA DECLINES 26%, PAT FALLS 43%; PROPRIETARY IMFL GROWS 39%, TARGETS ₹553 CR IMFL REVENUE BY FY30, 15–17% MARGINS & KERALA PLANT COMMISSIONING BY Q4 FY27

• Proprietary IMFL Business: Revenue grew 39% YoY to ₹57.7 Cr, with volumes rising 28% to 7.32 lakh cases.

• FY30 IMFL Guidance: Management targets proprietary IMFL revenue of approximately ₹553 Cr, with EBITDA margins of 15–17%.

• Kerala Volume Target: Aims to achieve 20 lakh cases in FY27, supported by distribution expansion and portfolio diversification.

• Kerala Manufacturing Expansion: Acquired SDF Industries for ₹30.85 Cr; 43 lakh cases annual bottling capacity, with operations targeted by Q4 FY27.

• Malt Plant Expansion: Commissioned 6,000 LPD malt facility, with captive consumption and third-party sales expected from Q3 FY28.

• Premium Portfolio Expansion: Entered tequila category with Arcana, initially launched in Madhya Pradesh, with expansion planned across other states.

• Central Province Brand: Q2 volumes increased 56%, with management targeting 10 lakh annual cases during 2027–2030.

• Geographical Expansion: Plans to enter Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh by FY27-end, strengthening its pan-India footprint.

• Ready-to-Drink Business: Kultur launched in five flavours, with expansion into Maharashtra and Rajasthan and registrations underway in four additional states.

• Ethanol Business: Q2 ethanol sales revenue declined 20% YoY to ₹56.6 Cr; segment EBITDA margin fell to 2% amid oversupply and higher grain costs.

• Ethanol Capacity: 130 KLPD installed capacity, operating at approximately 95% utilisation during H1 FY27.

• Capex Programme: PET bottling line and biogas plant targeted for commissioning by Q4 FY27, with the biogas facility expected to save 4–5% in power and fuel costs.

• Cash Flow: H1 FY27 operating cash flow stood at ₹65.6 Cr, supporting expansion through internal accruals.

• Management Outlook: Focused on premiumisation, proprietary brand expansion, Kerala manufacturing integration, in-house malt production and geographical diversification, while ethanol oversupply and raw material inflation remain key challenges.

VERANDA LEARNING SOLUTIONS Q2 FY27: REVENUE UP 17% YOY, EBITDA RISES 28%, PAT TURNS POSITIVE; GOVERNMENT TEST PREP GROWS 31%, J.K. SHAH COMMERCE DEMERGER COMPLETED & SEPARATE LISTING EXPECTED SHORTLY

• Net Profit: PAT before exceptional items turned positive at ₹13.4 Cr versus loss of ₹12.8 Cr YoY, supported by a ₹13.4 Cr tax credit.

• H1 FY27 Performance: Revenue grew 34% YoY to ₹104.1 Cr; EBITDA increased 39% to ₹24.4 Cr and PAT before exceptional items reached ₹25.6 Cr versus loss of ₹24.5 Cr.

• Government Test Prep: Revenue increased 31% YoY to ₹43 Cr, while EBITDA surged 79% to ₹10.7 Cr.

• Student Enrolments: H1 enrolments grew 12% YoY to 41,559, while collections increased 17% to ₹117 Cr.

• Government Test Prep Expansion: Opened new centres in Tenkasi and Dharmapuri, along with a new presence in Coimbatore.

• FY27 Expansion Plans: Management plans three additional offline centres in Tamil Nadu.

• Karnataka Expansion: Partnered with Dr. Rajkumar Academy of Civil Services, with new centres planned in Mysuru and Kalaburagi.

• Commerce Demerger: NCLT-approved demerger became effective on August 31, 2026, separating J.K. Shah Commerce Education.

• J.K. Shah Listing: Received in-principle NSE and BSE approvals and SEBI relaxation; management expects separate listing within approximately one week of November 13, 2026.

• Shareholder Entitlement: Eligible Veranda shareholders receive one J.K. Shah Commerce Education share for every Veranda share held as of October 6, 2026.

• Commerce Business: Delivered ₹53.05 Cr PAT during the five months ended August 2026, against its full-year ₹110 Cr PAT guidance.

• K12 Expansion: Plans to launch Veranda Sprouts preschool at Perumbakkam, with admissions beginning January 2027 and first batch commencing June 2027.

• Digital Expansion: Rolling out School Canvas ERP and expanding digital-led admissions, corporate partnerships and hiring collaborations.

• Management Outlook: Focused on profitable growth, test preparation expansion, K12 development, operating leverage and stronger capital allocation following the Commerce demerger.

GRE RENEW ENERTECH H1 FY27: REVENUE SURGES 216.7% YOY, EBITDA JUMPS 131.6%, PAT RISES 127.5%; ₹220 CR ORDER BOOK, 97+ MW PROJECTS UNDER EXECUTION & SOLAR PORTFOLIO CROSSES 197 MW

• Revenue: Surged 216.7% YoY to ₹138.7 Cr, driven by strong solar EPC project execution.

• EBITDA: Increased 131.6% YoY to ₹13.2 Cr, with margin declining to 9.52% from 13.01%.

• Net Profit: Jumped 127.5% YoY to ₹9.1 Cr, with PAT margin at 6.56%.

• Order Book: Strong confirmed order book of approximately ₹220.3 Cr, including GST, as of October 2026.

• Execution Pipeline: Over 97.2 MW of solar projects under execution, providing revenue visibility for the next 6–12 months.

• Solar Portfolio: Cumulative portfolio crossed 197 MW, supported by industrial, commercial and government projects.

• Major EPC Project: Secured a 50 MW AC / 65 MW DC solar project, contributing approximately 48% of H1 FY27 revenue.

• Margin Pressure: Large EPC project executed at lower margins to strengthen credentials for bigger projects and government tenders.

• Solar Commissioning: Completed 9.676 MW Himmatnagar project and an additional 2 MW subsidiary project.

• RESCO Expansion: Portfolio projected to reach approximately 15.5 MW in FY27, supporting recurring power-sale income.

• Long-Term Revenue: RESCO projects operate under 25-year power purchase agreements, providing annuity-like cash flows.

• Business Mix: EPC contributed 93% of H1 revenue, while RESCO accounted for approximately 2%.

• Geographical Expansion: Expanding beyond Gujarat into Rajasthan, Delhi and Maharashtra.

• Growth Strategy: Plans to scale utility-scale solar projects, expand into hybrid energy and battery energy storage systems (BESS), and strengthen O&M services.

• Financial Position: Trade receivables increased significantly to ₹80.2 Cr from ₹9.8 Cr in FY26, indicating higher working capital requirements.

• Management Outlook: Focused on executing its order book, increasing RESCO asset ownership, entering larger government tenders and expanding solar EPC operations across India.

India's net direct tax collections grew by 11.8% year-on-year to ₹14.42 lakh crore as of November 10, outpacing the budgeted growth pace.

INDO COUNT INDUSTRIES Q2 FY27: TOTAL INCOME SURGES 57% YOY, EBITDA JUMPS 111%, PAT RISES 238%; TARGETS ₹5,500 CR FY27 INCOME, 13% EBITDA MARGIN, 105–110 MN METRE VOLUMES & ₹8,000 CR REVENUE BY CY28

• Total Income: Increased 57% YoY to ₹1,699 Cr, achieving highest-ever quarterly income.

• EBITDA: Surged 111% YoY to ₹259 Cr, with margin expanding 380 bps to 15.3%.

• Net Profit: Jumped 238% YoY to ₹132 Cr, up 109% QoQ.

• H1 FY27 Performance: Total income increased 43% YoY to ₹2,923 Cr; EBITDA rose 73% to ₹420 Cr and PAT surged 150% to ₹195 Cr. FinancialFilings +1

• FY27 Income Guidance: Targets approximately ₹5,500 Cr, with management expecting to exceed guidance.

• FY27 EBITDA Margin Guidance: Maintains 13% target, already surpassed with H1 margin of 14.4%; management sees potential for 14–15% full-year margins.

• FY27 Volume Guidance: Targets 105–110 million metres, with 51 million metres achieved during H1.

• CY28 Growth Target: Aims to double FY25 revenue base of approximately ₹4,000 Cr to ₹8,000 Cr by CY28.

• Core Business: H1 revenue reached ₹2,033 Cr, representing approximately 50% of the ₹4,000 Cr FY27 target.

• New Business Expansion: Utility bedding and US branded businesses contributed ₹890 Cr during H1, achieving nearly 60% of the ₹1,500 Cr FY27 target. BazaarWatch +1

• Quarterly New Business: Revenue crossed ₹500 Cr, contributing approximately 30% of total income.

• Utility Bedding: Three manufacturing facilities achieved over 65% capacity utilisation, with full utilisation targeted by CY28.

• Wamsutta Brand Expansion: Expanding beyond direct-to-consumer channels into broader US retail distribution.

• Branded Business Target: Aims to achieve $100 Mn revenue by CY28.

• Export Diversification: Management expects non-US revenue growth exceeding 20% during FY27.

• Net Debt: Reduced to a record low of ₹518 Cr, with net debt-to-equity at 0.2x.

• Capex Plan: Approximately ₹250 Cr FY27 capex planned, primarily supporting spinning and infrastructure projects.

• Management Outlook: Expects H2 momentum to continue, driven by market share gains, increasing customer wallet share, branded business expansion and improving operating efficiencies.

ECORECO : DGFT BAN ON LITHIUM-ION BLACK MASS EXPORTS TO AID DOMESTIC FEEDSTOCK

• DGFT Notification 49/2026-27 dated 10 November 2026 shifted export policy for lithium-ion battery black mass (ITC HS 85491400) from Free to Prohibited with immediate effect
• Policy aims to retain critical minerals within India and strengthen domestic recycling, refining capacity and utilisation
• Ecoreco is among entities declared eligible under the Ministry of Mines ₹1,500 Cr incentive scheme for critical mineral recycling
• Company runs a dedicated lithium-ion battery recycling facility with 6,000 MTPA installed capacity at its Vasai plant
• Export prohibition expected to improve domestic black mass feedstock availability and support higher capacity utilisation and value-added mineral recovery
Impact: Positive (retaining black mass feedstock in India supports utilisation of Ecoreco's 6,000 MTPA battery recycling capacity and critical mineral recovery plans)

Viceroy Hotels Limited Delivers a Power-Packed H1 FY27
PAT Soars 2.7x | EBITDA Surges 81% | Total Income Up 61%
_₹105.83 Cr rights issue strengthens the balance sheet; net worth rises to ₹375.90 Cr, debt-to-equity improves to 0.70x_

Key Financial Highlights – Q2 & H1 FY27 (Consolidated)
Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26 (₹ Cr)
• Total Income: ₹48.79 Cr vs ₹31.86 Cr; Y-o-Y: 53.1%
• EBITDA: ₹12.89 Cr vs ₹8.82 Cr; Y-o-Y: 46.1%
• EBITDA Margin: 26.74% vs 28.64%; Y-o-Y: -190 bps
• PAT: ₹2.23 Cr vs ₹4.38 Cr; Y-o-Y: -49.1%
• PAT Margin: 4.63% vs 14.23%; Y-o-Y: -960 bps

H1 FY27 vs H1 FY26 (₹ Cr)
• Total Income: ₹93.99 Cr vs ₹58.31 Cr; Y-o-Y: 61.2%
• EBITDA: ₹24.68 Cr vs ₹13.64 Cr; Y-o-Y: 80.9%
• EBITDA Margin: 26.50% vs 24.29%; Y-o-Y: +221 bps
• PAT: ₹3.68 Cr vs ₹1.36 Cr; Y-o-Y: 170.7%
• PAT Margin: 3.95% vs 2.42%; Y-o-Y: +153 bps

Key Business Highlights – H1 FY27
* Half the year, half the job done: H1 FY27 EBITDA of ₹24.68 Cr is already 55% of full-year FY26 EBITDA; H1 Total Income of ₹93.99 Cr is 63% of FY26 Total Income.
* Momentum quarter on quarter: In Q2 FY27, consolidated Total Income grew 8.0%, EBITDA 9.3% and PAT 54.0% over Q1 FY27.
* Hotels growing at 21%: Standalone revenue from operations (Marriott Hyderabad and Courtyard by Marriott Hyderabad) grew 20.7% YoY to ₹67.81 Cr in H1 FY27.
* ₹105.83 Cr rights issue completed: 92,03,008 equity shares allotted on September 15, 2026 at ₹115 per share (incl. ₹105 premium), for debt repayment and general corporate purposes.
* A stronger balance sheet: As of Sept 30, 2026: net worth ₹375.90 Cr (from ₹266.80 Cr on Mar 31, 2026); cash and current investments ₹125.55 Cr; debt-to-equity 0.70x (from 0.99x).
* Executive Apartments fully integrated: Following a Novation Agreement executed on September 29, 2026, Marriott Executive Apartments operates in the name of Viceroy Hotels Limited from October 1, 2026.

SALZER ELECTRONICS Q2 FY27: REVENUE SURGES 38.4% YOY, EBITDA RISES 9.3%, PAT GROWS 11.1%; TARGETS 7.5–8% FY27 EBITDA MARGIN, 9–10% BY FY28, SAUDI PLANT COMMISSIONING IN APRIL 2027 & EXPORT SHARE ABOVE 25%

• Revenue: Increased 38.4% YoY to ₹579.77 Cr, supported by industrial switchgear, wires & cables and building electrical products.

• EBITDA: Rose 9.25% YoY to ₹39.95 Cr, with margin declining to 6.89% from 8.73% YoY.

• Net Profit: Increased 11.09% YoY to ₹14.87 Cr.

• H1 FY27 Performance: Revenue grew 25.32% YoY to ₹1,077.79 Cr, while EBITDA declined 9.03% to ₹71.26 Cr and PAT fell 24.21% to ₹23.20 Cr.

• FY27 Margin Guidance: Targets EBITDA margins of approximately 7.5–8%, improving towards 9–10% by FY28.

• Margin Recovery: Management expects gradual improvement from Q3–Q4 FY27, subject to stabilisation of copper, silver, aluminium and other raw material prices.

• Industrial Switchgear: Contributes approximately 55% of revenue, with segment EBITDA margin at 7.92% and a longer-term target of 12.5%.

• Wire & Cable Business: Contributes approximately 38% of revenue, targeting EBITDA margin improvement towards 6.5%.

• Export Guidance: Targets export contribution above 25% over the medium term, compared with 21.29% in H1 FY27.

• Saudi Arabia Expansion: Manufacturing facility commissioning targeted for April 2027, subject to easing geopolitical uncertainties.

• US Export Opportunity: Presentation highlights tariff reduction from 50% to 18% as a potential catalyst for export growth.

• Smart Meter Expansion: Commissioned 4 million units of annual capacity, with production ramp-up dependent on tender execution and consortium orders.

• EV Charging Business: Strategic investment of ₹8 Cr for a 30% stake in UltraFast Chargers; management aims to double EV charging revenue next year.

• Energy Management Project: Approximately ₹200 Cr Bengaluru BBMP project expected to generate ₹2–2.5 Cr monthly recurring revenue from February 2027.

• Capacity Utilisation: Industrial switchgear operating at approximately 80%, while wire and cable utilisation stands at 65%.

• Long-Term Growth Ambition: Management maintains its vision of doubling revenue and profitability every four years.

• Management Outlook: Positive on industrial electrification, export expansion, smart metering, EV charging and recurring energy-management revenue, with profitability recovery dependent on raw material stability.

**CLSA ON TATA POWER – HOLD | TARGET ₹415**

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Recurring PAT grew 51% YoY.
- Performance was broadly in-line with estimates.
- Indonesian coal supported earnings growth.
- Lower base benefited Mundra performance.
- Wind generation improved due to climatic conditions.
- Solar EPC and RE IPP PAT declined.

**Margin Pressure**
- Solar module and cell margins impacted 257 bps.
- Solar EPC margins remained under pressure.
- EPC margin decline stood at 410 bps.
- Continued margin pressure remains a concern.

**Key Positives**
- Indonesian coal mines PAT/tonne increased sevenfold.
- Higher seaborne coal prices drove profitability.
- Wind IPP business delivered strong performance.

**Key Monitorables**
- Solar manufacturing margin recovery.
- Solar EPC margin improvement.
- Renewable curtailment and IPP profitability.

**Impact: Mixed**

**GOLDMAN SACHS – FEDERAL BANK | BUY | TARGET ₹430**

**Management's RoA Targets**
- Q2 FY27 RoA stood at 1.3%.
- Immediate RoA target: 1.5%.
- Long-term RoA aspiration: 1.6–1.8%.

**Key RoA Improvement Drivers**
- Strengthening the liability franchise.
- Gradual diversification towards higher-yielding assets.
- Focus on mid-to-high yielding segments.
- Increasing fee income contribution.

**Acquisition & Growth Strategy**
- Prioritising core business strengthening.
- Open to smaller strategic acquisitions.
- Avoiding large-scale mergers currently.
- Large mergers could prolong integration.
- Integration risks could disrupt core performance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Focus remains on improving return ratios.
- Liability franchise and asset mix remain priorities.
- Smaller acquisitions preferred over large mergers.
- RoA improvement remains the key monitorable.

📊 BERNSTEIN ON INDIA STRATEGY | VENUGOPAL GARRE

• Nifty Target – Raises December 2026 target to 26,100 from 25,000.

• Ratings – Maintains near-term Trading Buy and 12-month Neutral stance.

• Near-Term Outlook – Easing Iran tensions, softer crude prices, lower bond yields and improving flows support a market rally.

• Earnings – Strong earnings momentum provides temporary support, but weak demand and limited earnings upgrades raise sustainability concerns.

• Medium-Term Risks – Expensive valuations, fiscal constraints and AI-related risks cloud the outlook.

• Preferred Sector – Financials remain Bernstein's preferred sector.

📊 JEFFERIES INDIA STRATEGY | ABHINAV SINHA

FPI FLOWS – POTENTIAL REVIVAL BENEFICIARIES

• FPI Flows – After persistent selling, foreign portfolio investor flows have recently turned positive.

• Key Triggers – Potential AI-trade reversal, equity tax relief, resilient domestic macro, reasonable large-cap valuations and light positioning could sustain inflows.

• Large-Cap Focus – Large caps could be the cleaner play on a revival in FPI flows.

• Valuations – Large-cap valuations have become more reasonable.

• Key Rationale – Higher liquidity and greater FPI ownership make large caps more direct beneficiaries of returning foreign flows.

Keep Going, 
Even if your progress Feels slow.

CITI on Bharti Airtel ; Buy, TP Rs 2390

In a notable reversal, Bharti has reinstated its Rs299 recharge plan 3 months after withdrawing it in Aug'26.

While earlier plan offered 1.5 GB/day of data, relaunched version provides 1 GB/day.

Move reflects Bharti's response to competitive pressures, as peers did not follow its earlier tariff action, as well as elevated churn during 2Q.

Churn increased from 2.6% to 2.9% qoq, resulting in net subscriber additions slowing sharply qoq from +3.3m to +0.7m

Decision underscores challenges of implementing unilateral tariff actions in prepaid smartphone segment, where competitive intensity remains highest

It suggests that pricing discipline is difficult to sustain without broader industry participation.

Note that based on certain assumptions around Bharti's subscriber mix, had estimated the Aug'26 move could potentially benefit ARPU by c.Rs4/mth (EPS benefit of c.2%).

Bharti recently reported ARPU improvement from Rs264 to Rs271 in 2Q.

CLSA ON ONGC ; HIGH CONVICTION OUTPERFORM, TARGET PRICE ₹405 (CMP ₹234.80)

• EBITDA and core PBT beat estimates by 7% and 4%, respectively.

• Declared interim dividend of ₹8/share, implying a 3.5% dividend yield.

• KG-98/2 and Daman projects expected to drive production volume growth in FY27–28.

CITI ON GLAND PHARMA ; MAINTAINS SELL, TARGET PRICE ₹2,360 (CMP ₹3,132.80)

• FY27 CONSTANT CURRENCY REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE RETAINED AT 15%.

• Cenexi expected to return to profitability from Q3 FY27.

• Citi believes current valuations already factor in significant growth and margin improvement.

GOLDMAN SACHS ON VOLTAS ; MAINTAINS SELL, TARGET PRICE ₹1,025 (CMP ₹1,056.50)

• UCP segment delivered strong volume growth, gaining market share in room ACs and Voltas Beko (Voltbek).

• UCP margin recovery remained below expectations despite strong volume growth.

• EMPS margins benefited from a one-off write-back, while the engineering business remained strong.

• October price hikes expected to support UCP margin improvement from Q4.

• TARGET IMPLIES 2.98% DOWNSIDE from the quoted CMP.

At $6.83 per watt, Mumbai is ranked as the second-cheapest major data center hub globally after Shanghai, costing less than half of Silicon Valley.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
